conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced: the PaperPie Brand Partner base going into Q2 (5,200 at May 31) points to a much smaller YoY revenue decline than Q1's -33%, but the headline will most likely still read 'revenue down, net loss wider' (no tax benefit any more), which is the headline this name sold -3.2% on in July; 6 of 7 prints fell. So p_up 40 on a 4.0% scale gives -0.8, while the findings net to -0.3 because the one positive (narrowing decline) and the negatives roughly offset. The gap is the reaction base rate, which sits in p_up, not in any finding.
bar: unsourced. No usable consensus exists: MarketBeat shows a Q1 FY27 'consensus' of $53.1m revenue / $0.41 EPS against an actual $4.76m / -$0.16, which is junk (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-9-educational-development-co-stock/). The only reference points are the prior-year Q2 FY26 (revenue $4.62m, pre-tax loss $1.75m, net loss $1.29m, EPS -$0.15, avg Brand Partners 5,800; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Results) and management's stated aim on the Q1 call to improve on last year's Q2 (no formal guidance). print_vs_bar_pct is my revenue estimate (~$4.25m) against the prior-year $4.62m, not against a market bar. Every size is capped small for this reason.

Not crowded; no squeeze mechanism. No option market (baseline options.status no_options_market), so no skew and no priced direction. findings.finding: The PaperPie Brand Partner base entering Q2 FY27 (Jun-Aug 2026) was 5,200 active partners at May 31 (up from 4,300 at Feb 28, the first sequential gain in about 10 quarters, held through quarter-end) against a prior-year Q2 average of 5,800; with Q1 revenue per average partner roughly flat YoY ($0.90k vs $0.92k) and Q2 FY26 at $0.80k per partner, Q2 FY27 revenue computes to roughly $4.0-4.5m against $4.62m a year ago, i.e. a decline of about 3-14% versus Q1's -33%; new titles (the first in about 18 months) were dropped mid-June, inside this quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-09) disclosed the 20% partner gain alongside revenue -33% and the stock fell -3.18%; Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09) revenue -29% on partners 5,800 vs 13,900 and it fell -9.94%. The one up print in 7 was +1.21% (2025-01-13). The name has not paid for good partner news.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no estimate on this name (the only aggregator 'consensus' is off by 10x), so nobody has published the partner-base arithmetic; if the market expected a narrowing decline the stock would not have drifted from $1.40 to a $1.30 pin into the print on heavy volume. The partner gain was public in July, so the fact is known; what is not visible is the YoY comparison it implies for Q2.
findings.independence: Q1 call transcript (CMO: summer is one of the lowest quarters; plan is to improve on last year's Q2; new titles dropped mid-June; multiple promotions planned), https://www.webull.com/news/15219109458093056 . Prior-year base from https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Results . Same company documents, not an independent series.

findings.finding: The bottom line will likely read worse YoY even if the operating loss narrows: Q2 FY26 net loss of $1.29m included a $455,500 tax benefit, and since Q1 FY27 the company books no benefit (valuation allowance up to $1.93m, Q1 tax expense $16,500 vs a $374,100 benefit); with pre-tax loss plausibly ~$1.3-1.6m (no bank interest after the Oct 2025 payoff, $1.2m annual G&A cut, offset by 10-year leaseback rent at $8.00/sq ft) the net loss lands around $1.3-1.6m, EPS about -$0.15 to -$0.19 vs -$0.15, repeating Q1's 'net loss widened' headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27: pre-tax loss flat at $1.4m but net loss widened to $(0.16) from $(0.13) on the same tax mechanics; stock -3.18% (baseline). No prior print where the bottom line improved bought the stock materially.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody models this name; the tax mechanics are in the 10-Q but a headline reader will see EPS flat-to-worse. If priced, a 'loss widened' headline would not move it; history says it does.
findings.independence: Prior-year tax benefit from the Q2 FY26 release, https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/269893/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Results . Shares the revenue arithmetic of finding 1 for the gross-margin leg; the tax leg is independent.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 10-Q states EDC did not meet Usborne's annual minimum purchase volumes and did not supply the required letter of credit, giving Usborne the right to terminate the exclusive US direct-sales agreement (no notice given), and Usborne refuses to pay a $1.0m FY2022 volume rebate (disputed, not recognized); Usborne inventory owned is $19.6m of $36.2m total inventory. Tonight's 10-Q will restate or update this; any change in status would be large, but there is no sign of one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The disclosure has run through multiple filings without a visible reaction; no print has carried a change in status.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as a standing overhang (the stock is 4.7% off its low at ~0.27x book); the unpriced part is only the small probability that the new 10-Q reports a notice or new terms. Sized at the tail probability, not the tail.
findings.independence: Usborne's own US FAQ confirms PaperPie is a separate EDC business and HarperCollins distributes Usborne to US retail (the discounted-retailer competition the 10-Q blames), https://faqs-us.usborne.com/article/892-is-usborne-the-same-company-as-paperpie . No 2026 news of termination found.

findings.finding: Liquidity going into the seasonally weakest quarter: cash $1.66m and restricted cash $0.15m at May 31, a $2.0m Regent Bank revolver (Prime+2%, maturing 2027-03-06, CEO personally guaranteed) undrawn, no going-concern language; Q1 operating cash flow +$0.56m came from inventory liquidation ($37.7m to $36.2m). A summer-quarter operating loss of ~$1.4m means cash holds only if inventory keeps converting; a revolver draw would show in tonight's balance sheet.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (Oct 2025) printed with the bank notice of default overhang and fell -9.94%; since the HQ sale-leaseback repaid ~$30m of BOKF debt, no print has carried financing stress.
findings.why_not_priced: Financing question answered as: the revolver funds working capital in a shrinking business, not a ramp, but it is undrawn and no going-concern flag exists, so this is near zero. A draw would be visible only in tonight's 10-Q.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 10-Q balance sheet and liquidity section, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/31667/000118518526002870/educ10q053126.htm (shares a document with findings 2 and 3).

findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself; filed at 0 because an unexplained microcap pin carries no sign (a bid absorbing supply at $1.30 limits downside, a seller capping at $1.31 limits upside).

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with; the findings are close to balanced and the lean comes from the name's own reaction history (6 of 7 prints down, median -3.2%) and a 'net loss widened' headline that is likely to repeat, so the net is a mild negative on a stock already sitting 4.7% above its 52-week low with a month-long pin at $1.30.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold the July partner-gain print -3.2%): partner-base finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): answered as working-capital revolver, undrawn, no going-concern language; liquidity finding moved from -0.3 to -0.1.
Rule 6 (unsourced bar): every finding already capped small; confirmed, nothing further moved.
Rule 5 (unexplained microcap drawdown worth 0): the price-pin finding stays at 0.
Rule 8 (thin coverage): no confirmed unpriced company number, so abs_move_pct left at 4.0 rather than raised; p_up unchanged at 40.
